key_insight: Water transport in anion exchange membranes is strongly coupled to swelling and deformation, so a fully coupled transport-mechanics model predicts hydration behavior more accurately than diffusion-only models.
engineering_relevance: For CO2 separation membranes, accounting for hydration-dependent diffusivity and mechanical feedback can improve design and prediction under nonuniform moisture conditions.
method: Transient finite element model of water transport in Fumasep FAA-3-50 membrane
Includes concentration-dependent diffusivity, hygroscopic swelling, and nonlinear viscoelasticity
Compares uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations
evidence_signal: The fully coupled model was validated against steady-state water-transport measurements across water-activity gradients and matched the observed hydration dependence best at intermediate hydration levels.
watch_item: The transport response remains mainly diffusion-driven, so added mechanical coupling improves predictions but may not dominate behavior in all operating regimes.
paper_title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
